the commission (es) mr president, thank you to all who have spoken, for your participation in this debate and for the ideas that have been put forward. unfortunately, we do not have enough time to go into all of them in depth, but i would like to highlight what i consider to be the essential points of the debate. i think we all agree that we are not satisfied with our level of growth, we want more level of growth. i would, however, draw attention to avoid simplistic comparisons. it is not easy to compare the united states with the european union without taking into account the starting points and the future obligations of one or the other area. it is not easy to compare monetary union with monetary non-union either. in any case, the fundamental question that arises today is whether the lisbon diagnosis is still valid, yes or no? i am convinced that the greatest potential for european growth depends primarily on two things: more jobs in europe and more productivity. and i think that diagnosis still holds true. if so, what is europe missing? i think it is not the diagnosis, i think what is failing is the implementation, the implementation of what we decided in lisbon. the commission's report, however, stresses that while we are dissatisfied with certain aspects, we have also made progress in others. we have certainly made progress in employment; we have not made as much progress in productivity. we have made progress in the internal market, but not as much as we would have liked. in the financial system, we have undoubtedly overcome obstacles to unify it, but not so much that we can talk about financial costs similar to those in the united states. we have put in place some additional elements that will certainly help. the growth initiative, in my view, is an important topic to relaunch some other aspects. in our proposals this year we emphasize those elements which can facilitate and achieve productivity gains. research and development is certainly an objective, but here too we have to define very precisely what we are talking about when we talk about research and development. the 3% of gdp figure is certainly similar to that in the united states, but the differentiation between public and private investment in research and development in europe and the united states already gives a higher figure for public investment in europe than in the united states. is the problem therefore only the number, or is it also our ability to work better together, to avoid overlapping activities and, in many cases, to generate additional attractiveness, an incentive effect for private activity? these are elements which i consider to be fundamental; in any case, i think these priorities are well chosen and correct. we must never forget that our lisbon strategy also has clear limits: we want to have a sustainable lisbon strategy and that implies a certain degree, a certain level of social production and also a certain level of environmental protection. from there some other points have emerged in the debate. i said no. it is a question of political will, basically national, to put into practice what we have agreed. is the stability and growth pact a problem or a positive element? i personally think that's a positive element. i believe that sound finance is a key element for long-term growth. does fiscal policy serve as a discretionary element to improve growth in the short term? in theory, in some cases, it can work with these criteria, but nevertheless, we must not forget some issues which i think are fundamental. firstly, the operation of budgets and automatic stabilizers in europe - much more dynamic than in the united states - means that each drop in activity is compensated by half a point in terms of budgetary deviation. it is true that we have a limit, the famous 3%. it is a reasonable limit; experience has shown us, and i am convinced that it is, that having a fiscal framework is good for the european union; i believe that this fiscal framework requires, given our problems of the future and our problems of population ageing, to achieve a medium-term budgetary balance; i believe that, in this medium-term budgetary balance, the 3% figure as a nominal reference is a key element if we want to have an efficient system that allows us to control what we are doing and allows us to cooperate with each other. that is why i think it is essential that we raise the problems of the future of the pact. i think the treaty is still valid, i think the basic ideas are still valid, but there are some areas where we need to improve. we must certainly improve the link between the economic policy guidelines and the pact. there is no doubt that our concern cannot be solely the issue of fiscal consolidation, but fiscal consolidation to achieve more growth, and of course this is closely linked to the broad economic policy guidelines and raises a second problem which we have identified in recent years and which is that part of the difficulties we have today are the result of not having behaved correctly at the right time of the economic cycle. we have introduced growth elements into the pact, and the november 2002 communication was in that direction, by giving greater weight to structural deficits. there are still some problems with this key element, which we are certainly prepared to discuss and debate. we believe that the problem of the future is of the utmost importance; in that sense debt must play a greater role in the pact, but not just debt, but all those future obligations which can undoubtedly have a negative impact on our long-term growth. elements such as population ageing and the financing needs of future obligations are fundamental. one last comment. i believe, as some of you have pointed out, that the need for national commitment to the implementation of the pact is fundamental. that means that perhaps the budgetary processes we currently have could be improved in the sense that the national parliaments themselves would be more involved in defining their own future obligations and in fulfilling the obligations to which we have finally committed ourselves. i think we have a good place to start. it is true that we would like to see more growth and it is true that our margin is limited. when the commission drew up its financial perspective, we tried to strike a balance between not exceeding our existing margin of manoeuvre - despite the additional obligations - and at the same time not increasing our current financial margin beyond what was strictly necessary. but we are aware that in the end the union budget is 1, 1.14, 1.24% and that the large element of public expenditure today is at national level. so without that cooperation at national level, we cannot move forward in that higher growth that we all want for europe.

(parliament adopted the legislative resolution) the spring european council is based on two key documents published in recent months. this is partly the commission's joint report on employment and partly the report of our task force on employment, which is referred to in paragraph 19 of this resolution. the motion for a resolution was drawn up by our political group among others and i fully support it. the two documents stress that a more decisive and active implementation of the lisbon agenda and the european employment strategy is a crucial prerequisite for consolidating economic recovery in europe. the six million new jobs created since 1999 are proof that we should continue along this path. however, there is a need to strengthen partnerships at all levels and also to strengthen governance, as pointed out by wim kok, to ensure even more effective implementation of reforms. the ever-increasing technological innovation and the globalisation of trade require the mobilisation of all europeans and all policies. as rapporteur for the committee on employment and social affairs, i want to see a growth momentum in europe and a greater focus on economic development in the context of the 2004 employment guidelines. community funding for job creation, especially through the european social fund, should be more visible to citizens, so that the eu appears as a 'project-maker'.
the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter, but it is not yet clear whether the commission will take a decision on the matter. the breakdown of the basic environmental rules is due to decades of western productivism which has not relied on sustainability and has obscured a number of indicators, including the ecological indicators. we are seeing increasing evidence of this in the form of climate change, the decline of biodiversity and the rise of pollution-related diseases. these phenomena are alarming, not least because they are irreversible. they are so widespread that they should in future be central to the overall management of community policies, which implies at the same time a radical change in outdated economic, financial or social aspects. the spring summit should mark the beginning of a new era. it should be recognised that there is an urgent need to ensure an energy policy shift towards renewable, sustainable and economic sources of energy. if we can break the back-storm and reverse the traditional activities that generate and pollute, a new generation of jobs will be born: jobs in public services, in the tertiary and social sectors, freed from the time-related straitjacket, the precarious employment conditions that characterize certain sectors, or medieval discriminatory practices. as evidence of the demise of these outdated ways of thinking and working, there is a need to reform the environmental tax and the underlying taxation practices and to pave the way for a new approach in the form of a common economic policy that breaks the unholy alliance between economic growth and the use of resources.
in the light of the recent developments in the field of the internal market, the commission has decided to propose a new regulation on the internal market for telecommunications services. the european leaders may promise gold and green forests, but the beautiful words cannot hide the harsh reality. the lisbon strategy has in fact only resulted in a series of attacks on workers. the eu has not been able to cope with redundancies linked to stock exchange rates, closures and social plans. even more scandalous is the fact that public funds have been used to increase the dividend paid to shareholders in companies such as stmicroelectronics. the eu has not secured the necessary means to combat dishonest employers such as those who have been at the head of the parmalat company. on the contrary, it continues to protect tax havens and to maintain banking secrecy. lisbon has mainly resulted in structural reforms in the labour market, due to flexibility, precarious employment conditions and wage restraint. finally, the strategy has resulted in public services being subject to market forces to the detriment of the population. this is the background to the fact that the 2004 spring european council should mark a radical break with the lisbon process. the joint motion for a resolution does not follow this course, which is why i voted against it.
the report by mr de gucht, which i am sure will be of great interest to the house, is a report which is a good one, and i am sure that the commission will be able to support it. it is unrealistic, however, to suggest that the democratic deficit in the conduct of economic policy can be eliminated by involving the european parliament in the preparations for the spring summits. we should also reject giving the european commission greater powers in the coordination of economic policies. the commission has shown that it has too broad powers by challenging the decision taken by the ecofin ministers in november 2003 to lift the sanctions against france and germany for excessive budget deficits. the criteria set out in the stability and growth pact cannot be justified by economic considerations and should be abolished in order to allow member states to pursue fiscal policies that are growth-friendly. finally, we cannot accept that the environment should be the only priority area in the context of the sustainable development of europe's economy. the citizens and rural areas of the member states are thus left out of the picture. they are victims of unemployment and depopulation. let us ensure that citizens play the role they rightly should in the social economy by giving priority to employment.

commission. mr president, this proposal for a directive on the enforcement of intellectual property rights represents one of the main elements of a commission action plan of november 2000 to combat counterfeiting and piracy, and complements the recent customs regulation. counterfeiting and piracy are on the rise. they harm business, society and governments, as they are detrimental to innovation investment. consumers and rights-holders are not the only ones to suffer. member states are deprived of considerable amounts in lost taxation, and employment suffers when the business world is not flourishing. there is also a genuine threat to public order. counterfeiting and piracy carried out on a commercial scale are nowadays believed to be even more attractive than drug trafficking, and its perpetrators are linked more and more to large-scale organised crime. this proposed directive is the community's answer to this threat. it is not an easy proposal since it touches upon issues which involve many interests, sectors and different ministries in member states, for instance culture, trade and industry, economy and justice. there has been some very sensitive, sometimes emotional, lobbying both for and against this directive, and i appreciate the sense of responsibility that parliament has shown in the face of this pressure. however, the need for action is clear and not in dispute. the commission believes that, with the text agreed by coreper on 16 february, we have reached the right moment for a positive decision. the compromise text constitutes an appropriate balance among all interests involved, including rights-holders, commercial users, consumers and intermediaries. this balance has been achieved in a different way from that in the commission proposal, but it has been achieved. the proposal constitutes a considerable degree of harmonisation and it will provide us with an effective level playing field on sanctions and remedies. this will be essential for creating a business environment where legal players are not disturbed by counterfeiters and pirates. this fulfils the commitments made by both the commission and the european parliament in a communication of november 2000, which resulted from consultations carried out in the context of a green paper in 1998. it also contributes to the achievement of the lisbon agenda. in view of the safeguarding of the necessary balance and effectiveness of this proposal, the commission supports the text on the table today, as proposed via the compromise amendments jointly tabled by four political groups. the compromise text is thus the result of joint and very intensive efforts from all three institutions. i would like to take this opportunity to thank the european parliament as a compromise text: amendments nos 1 to 52 and 56 to 100. amendments nos 53 to 55 and 103 to 113 deviate from the text and must be rejected. the commission feels that these amendments would not contribute to the balance and effectiveness that has been achieved in the compromise and, in particular, would not be in conformity with the horizontal approach. the directive should apply to infringements of all intellectual property rights. in recognition of the harmful nature of counterfeiting and piracy, time should not be lost. the commission would encourage the european parliament to vote favourably on the council compromise text so as to avoid any delay that would otherwise arise and would only serve the purpose of those trying to profit from illegal practices. time will not improve this text.
the rapporteur. - mr byrne, as you said, counterfeiting and piracy are increasing exponentially, and it is vital for our economy that we have the necessary instruments to ensure that intellectual property rights are respected. it should be recalled that the commission presented its text in january 2003 and that this initiative had been expected since 1998, when the green paper was published. parliament has repeatedly demonstrated its willingness to act against counterfeiting and piracy by unanimously voting a resolution on this green paper and signing a written declaration. conscious of this need, the committee on legal affairs and the internal market adopted the amended report on the respect of intellectual property rights on 27 november 2003 by 28 votes to 3. the imperatives of the time and the urgency, on the eve of enlargement, of ensuring harmonised legislation to ensure that intellectual property rights, innovation and creativity are respected in the twenty-five countries of the community, led us to an original procedure. at the instigation of the council presidency, an informal trilogue has been meeting for the past three months to find a compromise. in addition to the council and the commission, your rapporteur, the rapporteur for opinion, the chairman of the committee on industry, foreign trade, research and energy and the non-attached rapporteurs, who i thank for their help and diligence, have also taken part in this procedure. this early conciliation was made possible by the extremely helpful irish presidency, to which i would like to express my particular thanks. i cannot forget the commission, which has continually assisted us with its expertise. the amendments tabled today on behalf of the epp, pse, eldr and un take exactly the same line as the council's compromise text. it is extremely balanced, fair, proportionate and confirms the message we were holding about the importance of intellectual property rights. the concerns expressed by parliament on behalf of many sectors have been taken into account. many safeguards have been introduced. they protect the interests of rightholders and consumers alike. the scope of the directive, in accordance with the international agreements to which the community is party, remains extended to any infringement of intellectual property rights. but from now on, only actions on a commercial scale will be reprehensible. the definition of commercial scale excludes acts committed by bona fide final consumers who do not act with the aim of obtaining a direct or indirect economic or commercial advantage. this extension of the scope does not affect any of the sectoral directives already adopted on copyright, electronic commerce and computer programmes. the private copying exception is even more strongly enforced. the other important points in the text concern the need to take account of the rights of the defence. article 8 on interim measures, in particular, guarantees the right of defence by limiting the time for bringing legal proceedings and providing for compensation for the defendant. the protection of personal data is upheld, justification and proportionality must characterize any measures taken, ensuring that no barriers to legitimate trade and competition are created. the specific nature of each case and the intentionality or unintentionality of each infringement must be assessed by the judicial authorities. all the measures taken are civil and administrative sanctions. the compromise is open to future revision, particularly in the light of developments in community legislation. if you accept the compromise amendments proposed to you, this directive could be adopted at first reading before the end of the parliamentary term. this will demonstrate the effectiveness of the work of the three institutions, be a sign of integration for the enlarged europe and strengthen confidence in the internal market. this is what we need to meet the challenge of the lisbon objectives and make our innovation-driven european economy the most competitive in the world.

in the case of the european parliament, the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. on this last point, it can be argued that the regulation infringes article 202 of the treaty establishing the european community, which provides that implementing powers may be conferred on the commission but not on the european parliament. it also infringes article 198 of the treaty, which provides that 'unless otherwise provided in this treaty, the european parliament shall act by an absolute majority of the votes cast'. however, the provision in article 5 of the regulation provides that the european parliament shall verify whether the conditions for financing are fulfilled 'by a majority of its members', although article 191 of the treaty does not give the european parliament the power to do so. that's why it's illegal, of course. the dimitrakopoulos report seeks to correct this mismatch by reintroducing the requirement of a 'majority vote' in the rules of procedure of the european parliament. but that only adds to the confusion and doubles the contradictions. we must hope that all these errors will give the court of justice cause to declare that this inconvenient and bad regulation is contrary to the treaty.

in writing. - (fr) there are three reasons why we reject the creation of an agency for the management of the external borders, which should be independent and have its own legal status. firstly, the management of land, sea and air borders is a matter for the sovereign competence of the member states. they must work hand in hand with the flows of immigrants and the fight against human trafficking. the council of ministers is also unanimous on this subject. secondly, each member state should have a representative on the board of directors, where decisions should be taken unanimously and not merely by majority vote. to our surprise, france was the only country to propose a board of just 12 members, which would deprive the member states of their right to manage their own borders. finally, we do not believe that the agency should have exclusive powers in these matters, particularly in the field of the return of illegal immigrants from third countries and the creation of a european border guard. the united kingdom and ireland have made a good choice in refusing to join the schengen convention on external border controls. the french government should have had the courage to do the same.

- mr president, commissioner, the proposal for reform of the tobacco cmo presented by the european commission is based on a wrong premise. the commission intends to make the total abolition of public aid to european tobacco producers a central element of the fight against smoking. the link might be worth examining if europe dominated the market completely and produced 95% of the world's tobacco. but this is not the case: europe produces only 5% of the world's tobacco and its production covers less than 30% of its needs. moreover, as the fao, an expert on the subject, points out, public policy aimed at reducing excessive tobacco consumption must focus on behaviour rather than product, on demand rather than supply. it must, in good faith, inform and prohibit. but if - and i quote our rapporteur - 'smoking, producing and selling crop products is legal, the commission's proposal will obviously only result in the manufacturing industries being forced to source outside the european union'. to undertake to eliminate european production as the commission is doing, while the european consumer market remains a very important and growing market, is to offer the whole of this market on a platter to our competitors, to non-european tobacco producers. brazil, whose production is exploding, is waiting for this. however, the manufacturing industries emphasize the essential role played by european tobacco in their blends. european producers have focused on varieties that are fairly neutral in terms of flavour but with very low levels of alkaloids. i am thinking, for example, of the virginie of vendée, the poitou-charentes, the atlantic loire. it is therefore tobacco grown in europe that enables european cigarette manufacturers to meet the increasingly stringent health standards for nicotine and tar levels that we are imposing on them. if we deprive them of this perfectly traced source, where will our industrialists go to source? in southeast asia? but what are the public health benefits? it should be noted that the disappearance of production leads, in this sector as in many others, to the relocation of processing. altadis is already closing sites in france and moving to morocco. is this the kind of development the commission wants to systematize? the european commission has not taken into account the socio-economic impact and the consequences for the planning of the territory of the measures it proposes. however, it is a very localised crop, often grown in sensitive areas where alternative crops are not always possible. it is an activity that creates many permanent and seasonal jobs. the reform as proposed can only lead to the complete abandonment of tobacco growing in all production areas and thus to unemployment. we must therefore reject this reform, reject its logic, that of the outright, discriminatory eradication of a production, community tobacco farming, reject its ideological, moralising, simplistic inspiration. the counter-proposal of our committee on agriculture is undoubtedly better. it is certainly in line with the commission's decoupling approach, but it tends to limit its scope and negative effects as much as possible. the recoupment of aid to 70% of current support will not prevent a decline in production, but it may limit the extent of the decline. the farmer was free either to continue his production activity - which the commission's proposal did not allow - or to consider conversion without jeopardising the balance of his holding. the commission's proposal is part of the overall cap budgetary framework as it is adopted until 2013. the commission's illusory recourse to the second pillar is clearly and fortunately rejected. the system of production instalments, which created disparities in treatment between producers and made the system excessively complicated, is wisely abandoned. maximum coupling, a high degree of subsidiarity left to the member states to apply the system in accordance with the realities on the ground and with the support of producer groups, is a real alternative, mr president, which our committee on agriculture proposes in order to maintain culture in europe as long as the consumer market is there. this is the right direction, and we will support it.

mr president, a green and hygienic majority voted against tobacco growing and - for some reason - against olive growing as well. all this because of a simple syllogism: tobacco causes lung cancer, so all you have to do to eliminate lung cancer is to stop growing tobacco. unfortunately, 75% of the tobacco smoked in europe, or 540 000 tonnes, is imported, particularly from brazil. so even if we eliminate our 350 000 tonnes of european tobacco, of which 25 000 tonnes are french, we will not change anything about cancer. on the contrary, in the case of france, more than 50 000 jobs would be destabilized, in sarlat, tonneins, lille and elsewhere. in europe, nearly 500 000 jobs, often those of manual workers - with fewer resources and therefore fewer means to fight cancer - would be threatened. so why this doodle policy? because the european commission does not like tobacco growers, wine growers, olive growers and farmers. in brussels, we are in favour of foreign agricultural preference and therefore preference for imported lung cancer.

- the next item is the report (a5-0058/2004) by mr gillig, on behalf of the committee on employment and social affairs, on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation amending council regulation (eec) no 1408/71 on the application of social security schemes to employed persons, to self-employed persons and to members of their families moving within the community, and council regulation (eec) no 574/72 laying down the procedure for implementing regulation (eec) no 1408/71 (com (2003) 468 - c5-0368/2003 - 2003/0184 (cod)). i give the floor to mr solbes mira on behalf of the commission. commissioner, allow me to express my deepest sympathy with you on account of your nationality.
the rapporteur. - madam president, allow me to begin by expressing my deep sympathy with what is happening in your country. ladies and gentlemen, this report, which concerns the updating of regulation 1408/71 and the regulation laying down the detailed rules for its application, is therefore being discussed today in this parliament. the amendments proposed to us - as has just been mentioned - are intended, on the one hand, to incorporate into the text the developments which have occurred in the various social security systems and, on the other hand, essentially, to incorporate decisions of the court of justice of the european communities, where the latter has had to pronounce on these matters. it should be recalled that the question of updating or general modernisation of the regulation is currently under debate, but also that on many occasions our parliament has asked for a comprehensive revision of the regulations on the coordination of social security schemes. the proposal we are considering today is essentially aimed at updating the list of so-called non-exportable benefits contained in annex iia to the regulation. the judgments of the court of justice have made it possible to identify two essential characteristics which must be met by such benefits in order to be considered as non-exportable and thus to derogate from the general principle of the exportability of social benefits: their special nature in the state concerned, the fact that they are received in a situation of non-contributibility of the recipient - in other words, the fact that they are paid free of charge and on the basis of the general taxation of the state concerned - and, finally, a complementary element, the fact that the amount is a function of the minimum income necessary to live in the economic environment of the country granting them. in practical terms, non-exportable benefits may be considered to be certain supplementary resources paid to elderly persons or intended to compensate for transport costs, or disability-related benefits. it should be noted that, in general, all such allowances, when they are not exportable, end up in other member states in a similar way and are therefore likely to be collected at that time. what is the meaning of this update? we believe that the proposal we are being given is very positive. first, it effectively makes it possible to limit the exceptions to this general principle of exportability by the strict application of the 'special' and 'non-contributory' criteria. when we leave the exceptional systems, the conditions are always more favourable for all those concerned. secondly, this proposal puts an end to the divergent interpretations of the various national administrations and thus ensures legal certainty for employees who have to move within the european union. it brings transparency and clarity to an area which, as we know, is extremely complex, since it straddles the boundaries between what appear to be social security benefits in the strictest sense and social action, which is a non-compulsory element set up by the states. this is where the discussion should be and where all interpretations are possible. thirdly, this proposal must be adopted without delay to avoid further litigation in this very sensitive area for the citizens of the european union. we know that this question sometimes distances the citizens of the european union from each other on a social level, since they do not think that the union is responding as quickly as it should to the unification of the situation of all. finally, it is an element which facilitates and promotes the progress expected in the current general revision of regulation 1408/71. however, we must make a reservation concerning the specific situation of one of the member states which has seen, not the removal of a benefit, but the reintroduction of a benefit in the category of non-exportable benefits, whereas in the past it could be exported. we believe that this situation should lead to a more thorough study of the citizens concerned. they seem to be few in number, but the mere fact that some may be harmed would, in our view, require the consideration of a transitional period and further bilateral negotiations, when cases arise. for this reason, madam president, i will have to introduce an oral amendment at the time of the vote as an additional recital to go along with the amendments proposed by my colleagues, which the commission tells us it cannot accept. this was also the position adopted in the committee on employment and social affairs. this oral amendment should allow us to move forward. i would like to conclude, madam president, by pointing out that in this case we are faced with delicate balances linked to the procedure used. it is this open method of coordination that is fragile. we must preserve the progress it produces, when it produces it, as it does here. that is why i want this report to be adopted.
- mr president, on behalf of the french members of parliament, i would like to express our condolences to the spanish government, to our colleagues in parliament and to you, mr commissioner. i come now to the text before us. first of all, let me congratulate the rapporteur on having succeeded in drawing up a balanced text on a sensitive subject which seems to me to be satisfactory for employed ensuring better mobility for our citizens. it also relies on the judgments of the court of justice defining the non-exportability of certain benefits. these have three characteristics: their must be understood that in a social benefit system there are, on the one hand, so-called statutory benefits which fall within the scope of retirement and sickness and, on the other hand, another type of benefit called noncontributory benefits, which in france are called voluntary benefits. all countries have these types of benefits. when i was in france, i had social responsibilities and created a benefit: the parental presence allowance. for families suddenly faced with a disabled child, we had set up a benefit in paris of around 500 euros per month for 12 months. this benefit is - the next item is the statement by the commission on haiti. i give the floor to commissioner solbes mira on behalf of the commission.
- mr president, i was completely baffled when i read the draft resolution of our assembly on the situation in haiti. i was expecting congratulations from france and the united states - but especially from france, a european country - for putting an end to an insurrectionary crisis which was visibly degenerating into a very serious civil war. i did not see this congratulatory note in the draft resolution, even though the european union has been expressing great concern for several weeks about the outbreaks of violence in haiti and has asked all political actors without exception - i quote the presidency's statement of 18 february - to refrain from any form of violent behaviour. these platonic appeals have produced no results, whereas france and the united states have at least one. i also expected congratulations to france for not having cowardly disinterested itself in a country with which it has longstanding cultural and emotional ties, even though that country is located in the immediate vicinity of the united states. france intends to show that it remains aware of its historical commitments and the european parliament could have supported this responsible behaviour. i also expected congratulations to be given to france for implementing preventive diplomacy, an action which the european union, if it had been a good player, could have backed. instead, the resolution before us seems to regret above all, without daring to say so clearly, that a european country has taken the initiative without remaining perpetually in the ranks of those who make platonic appeals. it is a negative and regrettable attitude which is leading the draft resolution to surprising twists and turns. for example, i see in recital (f) that the conditions for the departure of jean bertrand aristide are veiledly criticised and that he is described as a democratically elected president, even though everyone knows, and the resolution itself recalls in recital (h), that the election for his second term was held without the participation of the opposition, which protested against the counting of votes in the previous parliamentary elections, thus creating a crisis which has only grown and degenerated since then. i also see in paragraph 11 that the european parliament would ask that the interim multinational force, authorized by the united nations security council, be made up not of french, american and canadian military personnel but of un peacekeepers, as if the european parliament wanted above all, as if the european parliament had only one obsession, to eliminate from this force the countries which have a presence in the region, whereas they are the first to be interested. in conclusion, mr president, i regret that the draft resolution fails to recognize that france has acted in the service of the law and the general interest, that it has assisted a people in danger - to avoid the worst - and that it defends the sovereignty of the haitian people, that it is also trying to defend the legitimacy of the process of political restoration. i would stress that the council of seven wise men, representative of the diversity of haitian society, has just appointed a prime minister, mr latortue, with the approval of the interim president, mr alexandre, which, by the way, makes recital k of the draft resolution a little outdated. this recent decision should be welcomed as part of a process of reconciliation and paves the way for the formation of a transitional national unity government, which will itself be responsible for preparing the next elections.
the commission (es) mr president, i thank the speakers for their comments. i would just like to mention two additional elements. firstly, in its statement of 1 march, the council clearly stated its support for the creation of a provisional multinational force to be deployed in haiti, thus supporting the united nations council. secondly, as regards the possibility of using the funds of the eighth edf, the union has made the normalisation of relations conditional on compliance with the necessary conditions and measures defined by the resolutions of the organization of american states, and we are continuing to work towards that end. in the meantime, in collaboration with caricom, we are prepared not only to provide the humanitarian aid funds that were provided for, but the additional amounts that may be needed.

- the next item is the statement by the commission on the impact of active low-frequency sonar on the marine environment.
- mr president, ladies and gentlemen, concerning the use of low-frequency sonar, i will first raise three questions and then make a suggestion in conclusion. firstly, as the two previous members have mentioned, this question has been discussed here in this house on several occasions and we have already been told, in particular by commissioner solbes, that we need more information. we are now hearing that a study is being commissioned by a danish body, but we have been waiting for some additional information for a long time, which may seem a bit curious in the long run. in fact, if the precautionary principle is applied in accordance with the treaties, we already have enough evidence of serious risks arising from the use of these sonars, especially for whales. this justifies a moratorium on their use today, in order to collect the information needed to establish further scientific evidence. do we really always have to wait for the worst-case scenarios to happen before we act? secondly, we are well aware of the worrying state of fish stocks today, both in europe and globally. we have learned - not surprisingly - that there is evidence that the signals from these low frequency sonars affect the movements of shoals of fish, which can lead them into dangerous areas that threaten their very existence. can we afford to develop and use technology which, when tested in peacetime, risks exacerbating the loss of fish stocks? thirdly, the eu has taken the first steps towards a common defence policy and a common arms industry. this will undoubtedly have an impact on european research, industrial policy and, in general, the development of the union. at a time when our societies are increasingly demanding environmentally friendly solutions, we need to prove that europe, in continuity with the lisbon objectives, is capable of being a world leader in sustainable technologies. can we do this if we are unable to react effectively to the development and use of such suspicious technologies as low frequency sonar? in conclusion, it is imperative from the point of view of environmentally, socially and economically sustainable development that we make full use of our capacities as european parliamentarians to influence, by all means at our disposal, the fundamental collective choices that are taking place in the field of the arms industries. that is why i strongly urge my colleagues to support my proposal to conclude this debate with a resolution at our next session, right here in strasbourg. only then will parliament have a relevant position to communicate to the various actors.
the commission (es) mr president, the commission is sensitive to this problem. we are aware that the scientific evidence on the problems posed by this type of sonar is growing. however, we believe that a more thorough analysis of current scientific knowledge is essential, and that it will no doubt incorporate the advances that have already been made - such as those mentioned by mr medina ortega in his reference to the article by professors jepson and fernández. the commission will certainly have to take into account in its decision-making the aspects of its competence, the national responsibility for the habitat directives and the margin of manoeuvre that member states have to apply the precautionary principle and, of course, the specific reservation on military matters which should not deter our insistence on nato and the military authorities to give due attention to these problems, especially in those cases which do not raise specific problems in the short term.
- the report (a4-0325/2007) by mr van den bos, on behalf of the committee on foreign affairs and security, on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european community and the republic of moldova on the participation of the republic of moldova in the european economic area (eea) (com (2007) 0173 - c4-0325/2004 - 2004/0329 (cns))
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, our european union is expanding by bringing together, on its values and standards, the states of central and eastern europe that have been emancipated from decades of communist rule. this harmonization of political and economic contexts at the top, which is demanded and pursued by the applicant states, maintains the stability and prosperity of this european area. but enlargement has also brought to light and given us an understanding of a new neighbourhood on the edge of europe. ukraine is one of those european countries which is struggling to free itself from the bad reflexes and practices forged by sovietism in the last century. the contrast with a central and baltic europe normalizing and recovering its rights accentuates the democratic deficits, pluralist restrictions and economic precariousness that stagnate along this new neighbourhood. it is true that this social, political and economic divide between the two poles of the same europe requires the european union, in the context of its enlargement, to mobilise its action, its resources and initiatives and its mutual assistance in solidarity. but this disconnect between the enlarged union and its eastern neighbours also raises the question of the history of our european union with regard to these eastern cousins, for whom the community's attention has been too limited to securing its border and their nuclear arsenal. instead of calling today for the intensification of tacis programmes in ukraine, in order to restore a precarious stability at a low cost to this neighbour, why not have our solidarity, our programmes and our budgets more widely opened up to him as early as 1991? nevertheless, ukraine is fully involved in european identity and its government maintains its claim to its rightful place in the european union, despite the reluctance of the european union. the european union owes the ukrainian people a moral and political debt to mobilize all its efforts and resources to effectively restore the fundamental rights of thought, expression, association and political participation in that country. the european union's vigilance in ukraine, with regard to the country's detention facilities, and its presence at the forthcoming elections are therefore imperative. but as the enlargement process shows, there is no better foundation for the rule of law, democracy, human rights and the environment than within our european union, not on its doorstep. it will be at the cost of further enlargement: the reunification of our continent will be at that price.

the commission (es) mr president, the union has adopted a very firm common position on burma, which is to impose an arms embargo, suspend defence cooperation, suspend all bilateral aid other than strictly humanitarian aid, ban visas and freeze the assets of members of the military regime, members of the government, persons in collusion with them and their families. and high-level government visits have also been suspended. the council working party on asia has recently assessed the effectiveness of the measures and reviewed the various options open to the european union to respond to the current situation. at present, the response is mainly the application of targeted economic sanctions combined with a series of constructive strategies to determine how to pursue political dialogue with burma and neighbouring states. the council's groups are currently discussing the renewal of the common position on burma, which is due to be adopted by 29 april. although parliament must be aware that the commission cannot know in advance the outcome of the discussions currently taking place in the council, at this stage it cannot be ruled out that new sanctions specifically targeting the regime may be introduced, which may be in addition to or complement existing ones. the commission is still awaiting the release of aung san suu kyi, which in our view is an indispensable condition for genuine credibility to be given to progress in the reconciliation process. the commission therefore intends to continue and even increase its humanitarian aid to the population. at the moment, the humanitarian aid we are giving to the area, to the country and to the refugees in neighbouring countries amounts to 10 million euros a year. the international support forum for national reconciliation in burma was held on 15 december. the union supports the process opened up with the burma forum and considers that the union should participate in that process itself. this is indeed a very positive development and the commission hopes that the bangkok meeting can become a 'bangkok process', which will serve as an instrument to obtain a commitment from the international community. it is essential to support the work of ismael razali, the special envoy of the un secretary-general, who should facilitate the debate between the state council for peace and development and the other political actors. the commission welcomes mr razali's visit, scheduled for the beginning of march, which represents a last attempt to advance the process of reconciliation between the military government and the opposition led by aung san suu kyi. i would like to make one final comment on possible additional sanctions. as i said earlier, the common position is still pending revision. in the event that the government of burma does not introduce additional policy changes, this possibility will have to be considered. however, we must be very cautious, because the impact of these sanctions on trade and investment has to be assessed in terms of their impact on the poorest sections of the population. at the moment, some of the sanctions adopted by the united states have led to large redundancies in the clothing sector, which have mainly affected women workers, with a significant increase in the impact in terms of human trafficking and prostitution. the appropriate balance must therefore be struck between the necessary rapid response to changes in the political situation and any reaction which must be proportionate to the situation on the ground and cause the least possible harm to the most disadvantaged sections of the burmese population.

- madam president, thanks to the corrections made by the council, which theresa villiers deplores but accepts, we have reached a text for the directive on investment services, the isd, which all parties consider correct. i will not be a big mouth, but i still want to say that we are deciding on a mutation that we do not know very well where it leads us. by removing the concentration of orders rule where it still exists, we open up competition between three systems. will the conditions of competition be fair? it is clear that the city-based companies, and primarily the american ones, have done much to advance their interests. the risk is that they will capture a substantial share of the european market, to the detriment of other players, and thus exercise significant control over the means of financing of different countries in the union. however, the council and the commission have ensured a balance and have not exempted these companies from the transparency obligations. however, they will be exempted from this for transactions of a higher amount than the average. i am told that the small countries and even some large ones will still dominate the national market compartment, but i doubt that this sharing is viable and we do not know what the strategies of the different actors, including the stock exchanges, will be. are the general interest conditions well established? will we be able to discourage the abuses and insider trading which are increasing, or at any rate are likely to increase, and ensure a process of quality price formation? we can still doubt it. for example, above-average trading volumes that will be exempted from pre-trade transparency can reach 50% of the total for the most liquid shares on the paris market. our successors will thus have to monitor the implementation of an essential directive, which is complex but with uncertain balances. we must advise them to be extremely vigilant. as regards the directive on transparency obligations, we have reached an overall compromise, the result of good work. i would like to make a few reservations, however. the most positive aspect is, of course, the rejection of the requirement for quarterly accounts. also the fact that the law of the country of origin will not apply to the liability of issuers. however, our requests for full information on the economic dimensions of the company, on social and environmental impacts were rejected by the council and referred to a subsequent directive, as were our requirements for information on the remuneration of company directors. i think this is a mistake. but the most serious thing, and this is not the fault of the rapporteur or the directive, is that the quality of information depends fundamentally on accounting standards and that the situation in this area is extremely serious. when the european institutions gave full powers to the ias board and committed themselves to apply its rules as early as 2005, i think they made a very big mistake. measuring the fundamental value of companies, banks and insurance mainly at market prices - value renamed for the fair value circumstance - is a source of bias and fundamental uncertainty. i therefore ask that we be very firm against any bastard compromise on standards 39 and 42, that we urgently strengthen efrag and its resources and, if necessary, that we postpone the deadline of 2005.

- mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by saying that this directive was eagerly awaited. this has already been said, but the directive against racism and discrimination on the basis of ethnic origin was voted in 2000: we are therefore four years later. does that mean that nobody is interested in this question, it is possible. perhaps it is simply an extremely difficult subject. i also note that the commission had great difficulty in reaching agreement, that the programme had to be much broader, that it had to include education and the media and that all this disappeared in the final draft. i regret this because the responses to the media and discrimination in the media, which would be to say that self-regulation is enough - that is what the professionals told us - are not satisfactory: i believe that we can all testify here, in relation to our countries, that self-regulation is not enough. there are also provisions in the 'television without frontiers' directive to combat sexism in the media: the results could be better. the aspect we are dealing with now - housing, insurance, goods and services - is important; it is all the more important that as we listen to each other tonight and read this report and this draft, we understand how difficult it is to fight against these forms of discrimination. from this point of view, i do not want to complain, but rather i want to be happy that europe is doing better than any of our states and that it is trying to tackle an extremely difficult subject: namely, to fight against stereotypes in cases concerning the calculation of premiums or types of insurance. i think it is great that europe can now tackle a problem like this. it has been pointed out that, in the end, we are still very far from the truth, that we are still under the influence of stereotypes, that we are content to use stereotypes instead of, as has been said on several occasions, considering a range of representations and causes that would allow us to better approach the situation of individuals in relation to insurance: well, yes! i think we have to fight against stereotypes in insurance production and reasoning. it has been said that women are the losers. men might say that not all of them want to be considered as drivers, that not all of them are bad drivers. so it is both men and women who are affected if we succeed in producing equal representation in insurance.
the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have followed these speeches with great interest and i would like to thank the committee on women's rights and the committee on legal affairs and the internal market, the committee on civil liberties and the committee on employment and social affairs for their contributions to the report under discussion. i would like to congratulate mrs prets on her excellent report, which proposes many improvements to our proposal and gives it greater clarity and greater coherence with previous community directives. in particular, we welcome the amendments which bring the commission's proposal into line with directive 2000/43 on racial discrimination or directive 2002/73 on gender equality in employment. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i would also like to thank the committee on women's rights for the proposed amendment no 15, which clarifies the line between private pensions and employment pensions covered by the current employment directives. the amendments are also in line with the discussions in the council. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial instruments are used in a way that is compatible with the common market. i refer in particular to amendments nos 16, 19, 21, 24, 25, 28, 29, 34, 40 and the amendments tabled by the committee on the environment, public health and consumer protection. nor do we agree with the deletion of the exceptions provided for in article 1 (3), since it is necessary to maintain a limited number of exceptions in order for the directive to be applicable. the commission has already made a number of proposals. we cannot support the amendments extending the proposal to the fields of education, the media and advertising. the commission proposal focuses on one specific area, the goods and services sector. it is therefore a step-by-step approach in a field where everyone knows that there is a lot of discrimination based on sex, which can be eliminated by a binding legislative act. we recognise that gender representation in the media and advertising raises serious issues in terms of protecting the dignity of men and women and that in the field of education girls and boys are often discouraged from pursuing non-traditional paths, but other complex issues such as media freedom are raised. the commission therefore considers that a binding legislative act is not appropriate at this stage to address them. i refer to amendments nos 38 and 39. finally, as regards amendments nos 35 and 36, in article 4 of the proposal, we cannot agree to amendments which are intended to allow the use of sex-based weighting factors. the use of gender-based weighting factors is not compatible with the principle of equal treatment and therefore cannot be objectively justified. such proportional factors make broad generalizations about all men and all women and cannot be justified. they reflect statistics about the average population, but these statistics are misleading because they hide the fact that other lifestyle factors are more important than gender. in fact, studies have shown that 86 percent of men and women have the same life expectancy. in this 86% group, a woman is treated differently than a man under the same circumstances simply because an inaccurate generalization is made about the life expectancy of all women. this practice violates the principle of equal treatment and therefore cannot be justified by a generalisation based on statistics. however, we welcome the fact that the proposed amendment recognises that the cost of pregnancy in life insurance should be borne equally by men and women in order to comply with the principle of equal treatment. as regards amendments nos 10, 22 and 41, which propose, on the one hand, a reduction in the six-year transitional period provided for in article 4 in relation to the gender-based pro rata factors and, on the other hand, stricter monitoring obligations during this period, we do not agree with them because we believe that it is not possible to expect the insurance sector to adapt overnight and because we consider that an additional six-year period provided for in article 4 is needed in order to develop working methods for the use of other more precise factors instead of gender. however, we hope that at the end of this period the insurance industry will not have any difficulty in applying the principle of equal treatment and that european consumers will reap the benefits. as regards the amendments proposing to replace the term 'application of the principle of equal treatment between men and women' by the term 'application of equality between women and men' throughout the proposal, we cannot support these amendments because this would go beyond the legal basis of article 13 of the treaty. article 13 gives the community the power to combat discrimination, in other words to ensure equal treatment for men and women. it does not give it a broader mandate to promote equality or guarantee full equality in practice. although article 3 (2) of the treaty provides for the community's objective of promoting equality between men and women in all its activities, that provision cannot alter the nature of the legal basis of article 13 of the treaty. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect, and i am sure that the commission will be able to accept them. finally, mr president, on the last amendment tabled, no 45, which proposes that the member states should hold a dialogue not only with the non-governmental organizations involved in combating discrimination but also with the social partners, we agree in principle, but we believe that a broader wording should be adopted, covering all the actors involved, because there are other organizations representing social actors, such as consumer organizations, social organizations, etc. i am sorry that i have had to exceed my speaking time, but at least we have an optimistic side, because we see that we men will live about the same age as women.
- i'm sure you will, inspector. you have used your speaking time fully and very wisely.
the commission. the commission's proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling of foodstuffs is a very good one. the use of gender-based weighting factors is not compatible with the principle of equal treatment and should therefore be abolished in the framework of the directive. this directive is therefore based on article 13 of the treaty, with the aim of combating discrimination on grounds of sex. the aim of the directive is not to legislate the conditions for the functioning of the internal market and therefore article 95 is not the appropriate legal basis.

- mr president, commissioner, the incredibly detailed draft regulation we are debating this morning is a perfect example of a useless text. there are reasonable provisions governing the transport of animals and promoting their welfare, which is one of the characteristics of the european agricultural model. however, these provisions are not always properly applied and are not sufficiently controlled. but rather than seeking to improve this application and control, which is too obscure a task, the commission considers it more gratifying to embark once again on the regulatory leap forward by presenting us with this new paving stone, which takes up the most maximalist demands of the ideological lobbies under whose influence it is. i do not care what serious consequences his text may have for our transporters and farmers. this is clearly not the european commission's problem, which does not even bother, as it usually does, to accompany its legislative proposal with a study of the impact of the measures it proposes on the activities of the professionals concerned. we have spoken at length in the committee on agriculture and rural development about the angle of the ramps to the cattle stalls. is it not to exceed 33,33% of the horizontal or 30% for pigs, calves and horses and not to exceed 50% or 30% for sheep and cattle other than calves, provided that ramps are equipped with ramps at intervals of not more than 30 cm? the only remaining factor is the coefficient of friction of the hooves on the ramp. this gap will certainly be filled in the next draft regulation which the commission will submit to us. frankly, is it our role to impose such detailed regulations, to put our producers, our farmers, our transporters, our creators of wealth and jobs in such a refined box? is it not suicidal to impose such heavy burdens, such costly constraints on european economic agents alone in a context of free trade where we deprive ourselves of the instruments of regulation? is it not to work for the benefit of third countries, discouraging our own producers and favouring imports? despite the few common sense remarks made by the committee on agriculture, such as the need to slaughter livestock as close as possible to the place of production, the architecture and spirit of the commission's regulation remain essentially intact. that is why, mr president, we will oppose this harmful text.
commission. mr president, the purpose of this debate is to formulate an opinion for the guidance of the council and the commission in coming to a final conclusion in relation to this issue. certainly we have had a very wide expression of views and opinions from one side and the other on the issue, and i hope and expect that the council can draw some guidance from what has been said. allow me to express the commission’s opinion in relation to the main points of concern. on travelling times, the european parliament wants to introduce a fixed and final time limit of nine hours for slaughter animals, while allowing the others to travel with fewer restrictions. as i said at the outset, we cannot adopt measures which would effectively ban a trade, particularly in circumstances where there is insufficient scientific information to support such a move. in order to limit the transport of animals for slaughter, the european parliament advocates the use of mobile slaughterhouses. at present there is not enough expertise or practical experience to support this solution and the animal welfare advantages have not been clearly demonstrated. regarding the scope of the regulation, the european parliament suggests a derogation for journeys of less than 100 km, as well as for certain categories of animals such as animals transported for sporting events and shows. the commission could support retaining the current derogation for journeys of less than 50 km, but there is no reason to exclude from the scope of the regulation other animals that are at risk of suffering poor standards of welfare. the commission supports the proposal to open up the possibility for member states to adopt stricter national rules, provided that they are compatible with the general rules of the treaty. i am pleased that this would effectively maintain the uk’s restriction on the export of horses destined for human consumption. i have consistently said that i would look at this matter with a view to supporting a legally sustainable text. in relation to the authorisation of transporters and the pre-approval of vehicles, the european parliament proposes having a single system for short and long journeys. one of the major objectives of the proposal is to focus checks on long journeys – these are the most critical for the welfare of animals. i believe that by removing the distinction between long and short journeys, the efforts of inspection and the administrative burdens would be diluted and animals transported over long journeys would not benefit from a higher degree of attention from the competent authorities. the european parliament suggests introducing the use of a satellite navigation system. this idea is most innovative and the commission fully supports it in principle. i should add that the commission proposal already includes a requirement to check the vehicles’ tachographs as a new enforcement tool. as regards sanctions, a number of amendments have been proposed. most of the suggestions are already covered by the commission proposal through a stricter system of authorisation for transporters. a number of other amendments on sanctions need to be examined with regard to their compatibility with the principle of proportionality. a full listing of the commission’s position on each of the amendments is being made available to parliament and i trust that this will be included in the verbatim report of proceedings for this part-session commission's position on amendments by parliament: see annex..

- mr. president, doctors have known since hippocrates that our health is dependent on our environment. the various media reports of recent years only add to the public's concerns. the epidemiological landscape has changed radically today. it is dominated by cardiovascular disease, cancer, and allergic or respiratory diseases. the causes of these diseases are many, often complex and interacting with each other. they are sometimes uncertain or sometimes still unknown. however, it is clear that the environment, in the broadest sense, plays a major role. our physical environment is thus one of the main risk factors for the health of citizens. i shall not dwell here on the dangers of industrial and polluting sites or nuclear power stations. it is especially necessary, and this is already the case, to take better account of the immediate environment which causes thousands of cancers. chemical substances, electromagnetic waves and traffic-related urban and air pollution are major public health issues in europe. our behaviour and lifestyle are based on eating too much, and stress and work intensity are the cause of many health problems. so tobacco use, especially secondhand smoke and tobacco use among children, must be firmly opposed. strong regulations must be put in place today to ban smoking in workplaces and public places. in view of these challenges, we are concerned about the weakness of the commission's proposals. the greens call for a more concrete and ambitious strategy to meet the health challenges of the 21st century. that is the meaning of the amendments we have tabled. we need to address the problems at their source by proposing concrete actions today, while accepting the uncertainty inherent in scientific knowledge. it is therefore necessary that the strategy be strongly based on the principles of precaution and prevention. in this context, we call for a significant strengthening of the strategy for reducing risk exposure. the greens are calling for these major lines of thinking and action to be taken into account so that the european union can live up to the fears and expectations of our citizens and, above all, to the public health revolution we must achieve.
the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: - mr president, the question in today's debate is not whether or not we should adhere to the aarhus convention. the community signed this agreement in 1998, and it is now our responsibility to ensure that each of our governments can implement it. by signing the aarhus convention, the community committed itself to adopting legally binding instruments, a directive and a regulation respectively, with a view to aligning community legislation with the provisions of the aarhus convention. the committee worked with this essential conformity with the convention in mind. it is also in this spirit that the amendments tabled in plenary, which have received wide support, were drawn up. the work initially consisted in unifying the various concepts contained in the texts and adapting them to the definitions of this convention. on the other hand, we respected the choice of the executive commission to offer the possibility of litigation to non-governmental organisations active in the field of the environment, while opening this avenue more widely to qualified entities with legal personality. in the same spirit, we have made the objective of promoting sustainable development an essential condition in their statute for the exercise of the right to a fair trial. furthermore, only the provisions contained in the aarhus convention and the directive gave the right to bring legal proceedings to members of the public who claimed a breach of a right or who had an interest in acting. in order to ensure that the community institutions are bound by the same rules as the member states, we have endeavoured to incorporate this provision into this regulation. finally, we have always been committed to respecting the necessary subsidiarity of the member states in the area of judicial procedure. in so far as those questions concern the procedural law of the member states, they fall within the procedural autonomy of the member states and must not give rise to a binding legal instrument on the part of the union. moreover, it is not conceivable to introduce a specific mechanism, a kind of privileged right to litigation in environmental matters, which would be easier and less costly. it is essential that access to justice issues are dealt with in a comprehensive and coherent way in all areas, and not just specifically in the field of the environment. finally, some of the proposals in the working document go beyond the obligations arising from the aarhus convention. however, it is necessary to maintain the margin of manoeuvre which the convention gives to the member states for the implementation of these obligations. finally, i think we have reached a fair compromise which aims to promote, in accordance with the provisions of the aarhus convention, the effective implementation of community environmental legislation. if i may put it this way in conclusion, i would say the whole aarhus convention, but only the aarhus convention.
- mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we are dealing with two twin proposals which must both respond to the philosophy of the aarhus convention and only to it. adherence to the provisions of the aarhus convention is not on the agenda. what we must seek is to ensure that our governments and the community institutions are able to implement this agreement. the aarhus convention is undoubtedly a step forward in bringing about the transparency that has become indispensable, and we are here to present the modalities of public access to justice. but to be effective, the convention must be modern and involve all those who contribute to improving the environment in europe. it is therefore appropriate to introduce a specific reference to the concept of sustainable development. it would be inconsistent to want to be satisfied with a too restrictive definition of environmental law and thus to exclude entire sectors of activity which, however, play an active part in the achievement of our environmental objectives. i am thinking in particular of the trade unions. as regards the proposal for a directive in particular, since the aarhus convention will apply de facto, the first question is whether the directive is necessary. the questioning is legitimate and, if there is a directive, it must be in accordance with the spirit of the convention. in this case, it must also respect the principle of subsidiarity, which is the point of our amendments. it is indeed the member states which will have to implement the requirements of the aarhus convention and this will have to be done in accordance with the law in force and the legal traditions of each of our countries. i will not support amendments which seek to impose the judicial practices of one member state on all the others. on the other hand, we must anticipate possible crossborder cases and specify the possible means of redress. if these points are not included, then for reasons of legal consistency we will probably prefer to do without this directive.
- mr president, why would the implementation of the aarhus convention require specific legislation? we think it is sufficient on its own, which is why we have tabled a motion to reject the directive on access to justice. more importantly, this bill introduces unacceptable measures. first, the procedure for the internal review of acts adopted by the european institutions. what good will elected officials do if their decisions are constantly called into question by ngos selected by the european commission, which is also the guardian of the treaties? secondly, the commission's attempt to interfere in the organisation of national judicial systems, an illegal provision, since it is contrary to article 175 of the treaty. finally, the derogations from both civil and criminal procedure, which allow ngos to receive aid to set up a civil party and to be exempt from costs and damages to be paid in the event of failure, are morally unfair and legally shocking. in addition, to ensure sustainable development, i propose not to reserve the capacity to act to ngos alone, but to involve rural managers - landowners, farmers, foresters, businesses, etc. according to article 9 of the aarhus convention, it is up to the member states to organise access to justice. if adopted, this bill will inevitably generate difficulties in its implementation and legal uncertainty, which seems to me to be contrary to the objective pursued. the proper application of this convention requires respect for the principle of subsidiarity.
